answer: Quadratic slashing mandates anchor security by imposing super-linear capital requirements that penalize Sybil expansion through aggressive erosion of staked assets. While a single adversary may establish an isolated island of influence, the incremental burden of scaling collateral grows at a rate outpacing any possible value extraction. Consequently, the vast ocean of required liquidity ensures marginal attack costs exceed potential gains, forcing a Nash equilibrium characterized by negative expected utility for malicious actors.
